Taken literally, the rule can keep a start that violates the flotation equality over a feasible one, which contradicts AGENTS section 3 item 32 (flotation held to the solver's constraint tolerance in every reported state). C1 thin shell shows the case is real: both starts end infeasible (ratio pair 1-2 at 1.07e-5 and 7.13e-6) and the two possible rules pick different designs (fval 0.23418 vs 0.30249). The owner should decide how infeasible starts are compared; I did not enforce the literal rule.

summary:
Not accepted. The code itself is right: c_mono, c_mass_min and the leftovers listed in D14 and D15 are gone from both copies, the bottom-filled start is correct, each mode takes its upper density bound from its material input, and thin-shell t_min = t_init = 0.0254. I reproduced the suite (30 PASS, 0 FAIL, 2 SKIP) and the Stage-1 + Stage-2 C1 runs for both modes. Five things block acceptance.

(1) The code does not do what its comments and docs say when choosing between the two starts. run.m:135-137 and RUNTIME_GUIDE.md:170-172 say the start with the lower objective is kept. The code keeps a feasible start first, and when neither start is feasible it keeps the smaller violation. On C1 thin shell this keeps fval 0.30248618790013493 (violation 7.13e-6) over 0.23417953708632699 (violation 1.07e-5), with flotation inside 1e-8 in both. The rule departs from the owner's wording ("keep the lower objective") and was not flagged as an agent's decision.

(2) WEC_User_Input.m:44 and RUNTIME_GUIDE.md:256 say the thin-shell t_min "also sets the Stage-2 density floors". That is false at this commit: the thin-shell lower bounds are [20 20 20 20] whether t_min is 0.0254 or 0.2 (my test C).

(3) tests/README.md does not list tests/optim/ or test_stage2_c1_formulation.m.

(4) The report has a wrong claim. It says the precast start was chosen by a violation difference. In fact both starts are feasible and the choice is made by an fval difference of 4.31e-10.

(5) The new results field stage2_3d.starts is missing from RESULT_SCHEMA.md, and the report does not list it as deferred to T5.

The thin-shell exitflag -2 is listed as deferred with a reason (the ratio pair 1-2 is active while no thin-shell floor exists before T4b; the plan checks Stage-2 runs after J2). I accept that deferral.

Process note, not a required fix: contract section 4 says a task's shared-file edits are its last commit. Here 7ad75d5 holds them and a test-only commit, 4d6762b, follows.
